originality.rationale: The assessed result is a closed nilpotent Jordan partition and exact first-periodic-entry law for binary four-neighbor dynamics on a dyadic-by-arbitrary torus. The accessible 2D null-boundary, ternary periodic, and binary hybrid periodic primary texts do not prove the stated claim. A 2004 exceptional-rule paper remains an explicit, unresolved access risk; comparisons are limited to obtainable material, and failed retrieval is not treated as proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: Full primary text of Dihidar–Choudhury (2004) could contain a related or stronger result.
Only the abstract of Thomas–Stevens–Lettieri (2006) was accessible in the used public interface.
Unindexed or differently named earlier equivalent formulations cannot be excluded by semantic searches.

value.rationale: The sharp stopping-time distribution is a natural, complete finite-time invariant of a standard two-dimensional XOR rule, valid for every torus with one dyadic circumference. The odd-factor invariance and uniform nilpotent Jordan structure are structural, not merely isolated small-number computations. They can inform exact statistics and robustness analysis of additive torus dynamics.
